messages:
From: Rachel Stern <support@thetahealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime output freezing during peak demo - attaching pcap

Hi Marcus,

We ran a staged demo to 80 concurrent sessions this morning and saw repeated cases where the model output 'paused' mid-stream for ~12-22 seconds and then resumed. When the pause happens the chunked transfer stays open (browser console shows streaming: chunked encoding but no new chunks). Our front-end times out UI-side and retries which sometimes results in truncated responses. This is reproducible in ~3/10 of requests during the spike.

Attached is a short pcap and a small sample of request IDs (request_ids_0610.log). Key details: 2025-06-10 09:03:12-09:22 window (PST), region us-west-2, calls to /v1/realtime/stream with streaming=true.

We need an immediate mitigation (customer-facing fix or recommended fallback) and an ETA for a root-cause next steps update — this is on our pilot path to production and the execs are watching.

Thanks,
Rachel Stern
Support Lead, ThetaHealth
Rachel Stern | ThetaHealth

Rachel / Marcus — first-pass triage from infra: we see repeated TLS keepalive resets and segments where the kernel-level socket buffer for the proxy hits high watermark before the application resumes sending. On our side we observe a tight pattern of many small token-chunk writes followed by long pauses in the same request_id sequences you shared.

Preliminary hypotheses:
1) Intermittent backpressure caused by (client proxy) buffer fill + our continuous batching causing bursts of small writes, resulting in chunk assembly delay until the Nagle/flush window triggers.
2) HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer interaction with intermediary (your reverse proxy) causing the front-end to interpret the connection as stalled.

Immediate mitigations we can execute now (we need permission for a short-canary change):
- Deploy a temporary change to increase periodic heartbeat frames for streaming connections (will force periodic small chunks so front-end sees progress).
- As Marcus suggested, short-term disable streaming for the route (server-sent full-response) — releases you from platform-side mitigation if you control the client.

What we need from ThetaHealth:
- Exact reverse-proxy type and config, particularly proxy_buffering and keepalive_timeouts.
- A single session request ID and the time window to pull full traces.

I opened PD-7892 and attached the initial packet capture to the incident.
